name: Earth and environment: Measured rainfall–runoff transfer across catchments
description: Calibrate a causal, water-conserving snow/soil runoff model on measured CAMELS catchments and predict discharge in wholly unseen basins and a subsequent year.

sources.locator: CAMELS-US dataset description, catchment attributes, meteorological forcing and streamflow observations.
Official source data/evaluation reference; evaluator and seed independently written.

sources.title: Towards learning universal, regional, and local hydrological behaviors via machine learning applied to large-sample datasets
sources.locator: Develops rainfall-runoff models across CAMELS catchments and evaluates regional and ungauged-basin transfer. The local four-basin causal water-conserving model is a much smaller task-family adaptation.

requirements.datasets: SHA256-locked source bundle E01.json in .cache/science-earth-data. Automatically prepared by scripts/prepare_earth_data.py.

evaluation.benchmark: Earth and environment: Measured rainfall–runoff transfer across catchments
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_runoff(training_basins) -> callable runoff(forcing_history,basin_attributes,state). Daily forcing columns[precipitation_mm,mean_temperature_C,solar_Wm2]. Output dict discharge_mm>=0,evapotranspiration_mm>=0,state with total storage_mm>=0. Enforce storage_previous+P-Q-ET=storage_new to1e-5mm. Retrospective current-day forcing only; full unseen-basin/year holdout. Basin-macro NSE, extremes and water-balance diagnostics.

provenance.note: Local evaluator, candidate interface and seed recreated from scientific specifications; official benchmark data are reused.

limitations: Four source basins2000–2002; two training basins and two wholly unseen evaluation basins. Daily retrospective forcing, not meteorological forecasting. Tiny geographic sample is not the full671-basin benchmark.
Source data remain local caches with immutable revisions/content hashes and no evaluator network access. Public subsets are development-visible; freeze candidates before wider generalization tests.
Improved source benchmark performance is a scientific-method contribution, not alone a new discovery or operational forecast validation.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict catchment runoff across basins from meteorological forcing.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Hydrological prediction supports understanding of basin behavior and estimation of water availability.

papers.title: Towards learning universal, regional, and local hydrological behaviors via machine learning applied to large-sample datasets
papers.primary_goal: Predict runoff and investigate hydrological behaviors that transfer across catchments.
papers.task_relation: The paper directly models runoff across CAMELS basins. The local water-conserving model uses four observed basins and withheld basins/year; this restricted sample cannot reproduce the paper's broad regional-generalization results.
